In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

immunocytochemistry using broad-spectrum antikeratin mAbs may serve as a valuable additional method for the detection of occult hematogenous tumor cell dissemination in patients with SSC of head and neck region, but the prognostic significance of this finding remains to be determined.
immunocytologic detection and quantitation of isolated tumor cells is a promising tool for prognostication in patients with SSC of head and neck region.
immunocytochemical detection of tumor cells in bone marrows of patients with SSC is a promising approach to assess tumor spread and may be useful in the selection of patients for adjuvant therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of tumor cells in the bone marrow may be considered as a prognosticator in patients with SSC of head and neck region and that this approach is of value for clinical trials.
the detection of isolated tumor cell clusters in bone marrow aspirates is a valuable prognostic indicator of patients with SSC.
bone marrow analysis by immunocytology is a sensitive tool for detection of occult metastasis in patients with SCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunocytologic screening for isolated tumor cells in the bone marrow of patients at risk for hematogenous tumor cell dissemination may provide valuable prognostic information.
the immunocytochemical detection of isolated tumor cell clusters in bone marrow is feasible, but the clinical significance of these cells remains unclear.
the presence of A45-B/B 3-positive cells in the bone marrow of patients is a prognostic factor for poor survival, which was confirmed in a univariate and multivariate analysis of the data set.
